keyVerseText: They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course. out: Heb. moved
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun מוֹסָד (môwçâd) derives from the root יָסַד (yâçad), which means to found, establish, or lay a foundation. This root conveys the idea of setting something firmly and securely, whether physically or metaphorically. Thus, מוֹסָד carries the sense not merely of a physical foundation but also of an established base or principle upon which something rests, emphasizing stability and intentional establishment beyond the simple English term 'foundation.'
usageInScripture: The word מוֹסָד appears twice in the Hebrew Bible, consistently referring to foundational structures or principles. The top translations, 'all the foundations' and 'the foundations,' highlight its use in a plural or collective sense, often describing the fundamental supports of the earth or creation. This consistent usage underscores the term's role in expressing what undergirds and sustains reality, both physically and metaphorically.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מוֹסָד as a foundation rooted in the concept of establishment enriches our appreciation of God's creative and sustaining power. Scripture's use of this term to describe the earth's foundations points to God's sovereign act of ordaining and securing creation. For the Christian faith, this reminds believers that God is the ultimate foundation of all existence and truth, providing unshakable stability amid life's uncertainties. Moreover, it calls the church to be built upon the firm foundation of Christ, reflecting God's established order and faithfulness.
keyVerseReflection: Psalm 82:5 states, 'They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.' Here, מוֹסָד emphasizes the fundamental supports of the earth, which are described as 'moved' or disturbed, symbolizing disorder and instability. This use highlights the seriousness of spiritual ignorance and corruption, as the very bases of creation’s order are shaken. The word deepens the verse’s warning by portraying a world where the divinely appointed foundations no longer hold firm due to human failure.
